summary.oneLiner: Landmark FY26 — record Rs.2,421cr bookings (+25% YoY) on a blockbuster Gurugram Aaroham launch and 71% YoY realization jump — with management decisively pivoting incremental capital into a 50%+ CAGR senior-living vertical (Rs.6,500cr GDV launch queue), funded by customer advances on a low-debt/high-cash balance sheet; P&L still POCS-lagged but FY27 set up for 20%+ reported ROE.

one-line thesis: Landmark FY26 — record Rs.2,421cr bookings (+25% YoY) on a blockbuster Gurugram Aaroham launch and 71% YoY realization jump — with management decisively pivoting incremental capital into a 50%+ CAGR senior-living vertical (Rs.6,500cr GDV launch queue), funded by customer advances on a low-debt/high-cash balance sheet; P&L still POCS-lagged but FY27 set up for 20%+ reported ROE.
financial scorecard (real-estate kpis le:
**Bookings / pre-sales (the key metric):**
- **Q4 FY26 bookings value: Rs.1,290cr, +225% QoQ, +124% YoY** — driven by Ashiana Aaroham Phase-I & II (Gurugram) contributing ~Rs.833cr at launch (one-off launch spike).
- **FY26 bookings value: Rs.2,421cr, +25% YoY — highest ever.**
- **Senior Living bookings FY26: Rs.570cr, +55% YoY (record)**; from Rs.100cr to Rs.570cr over 5 yrs (~50%+ CAGR).

**Realization:**
- Q4 FY26: **Rs.11,566/sqft, +71% YoY** (Gurugram-skewed, not run-rate).
- FY26 full-year blended: **~Rs.9,000/sqft.** Even Jamshedpur/Jaipur now >Rs.7,000.

**Collections / cash flow:**
- Customer collections FY26: **Rs.1,762cr (all-time high).**
- Pre-tax operating cash flow: Q4 Rs.167cr (+7% YoY); **FY26 Rs.577cr (+34% YoY, highest ever).**

**Execution:**
- Equivalent area constructed (EAC): Q4 6.65 lakh sqft (+60% YoY); FY26 226.19 lakh sqft (+30% YoY).

**Reported P&L (POCS / handover-driven — misleading vs operations):**
- Q4: Total income Rs.335cr (+46% YoY); EBITDA Rs.35cr (+19%, 10.43% margin); PAT Rs.21cr (~flat YoY, 6.26% margin).
- FY26: Total income **Rs.1,187cr (>2x FY25)**; EBITDA Rs.176cr (+281% YoY, 14.85% margin); **PAT Rs.118cr vs Rs.18cr FY25 (9.93% margin).**

**One-offs:** Aaroham launch Rs.833cr booking spike (Q4); Project Maitri Kolkata dispute settled — Rs.18.5cr FNF received against security deposit; IFC Rs.100cr listed unsecured redeemable NCDs into Aaroham Gurugram. Consolidated revenue (Rs.1,140cr) > units delivered (Rs.988cr) due to (a) consolidated maintenance-services annuity and (b) top-up sales of leftover inventory in already-delivered projects.
guidance (critical):
- **FY27 pre-sales target: Rs.2,200cr** (note: below FY26's Rs.2,421cr, which was Aaroham-inflated — implies normalization, not a step-up on headline).
- **Senior Living FY27 target: cross Rs.700cr** (from Rs.570cr; the strategic priority).
- **Blended realization** to drift toward ~Rs.10,000/sqft (range Rs.9,000–11,000) as senior-living mix rises and Aaranya/Tattvam premiumize.
- **FY27 reported ROE: 20%+** (on track; cushion exists even at lower revenue if PAT margin held). Margin profile: FY27 > FY26, FY28 > FY27.
- **FY30: cumulative PAT Rs.2,000cr** target — "on track."
- **New launches this FY (FY27):** Ashiana Oma (Jaipur premium, approvals done, launch in ~2 months), Ashiana Aaranya & Ashiana Tattvam (both Q4 FY27); plus phase launches — Aaroham Phase-III, and ≥1 phase each in Advik, Amodh, Vatsalya, Swarang.
- **FY28 launches:** Wavarle, Vadgaon, Bangalore.
- Construction-cost guidance: **+8–10% YoY** in FY27 (higher than historical CPI; geopolitics-driven).
order book & pipeline (inventory, launch:
- **Land bank ~96 lakh sqft total ≈ 4x annual throughput** (~2.5m sqft/yr). Build-up: ~26 lakh sqft on deck Pg26 + ~40 lakh sqft ongoing phases (=66) + 20 lakh sqft Vadgaon (April, =86) + ~11 lakh sqft Bangalore (MoU, CP resolved, "99% likely", =96). Management calls 4x "just enough to maintain"; **actively targeting to add more land in FY27, mainly senior-living.**
- Senior Living **launch queue: 5 projects, GDV >Rs.6,500cr** (Chennai, Bangalore, Bombay-Pune) to launch over next 12–24 months.
- FY26 land added: Chennai + Maharashtra, >26 lakh sqft, ~Rs.3,200cr sale potential.
- Q4 BD: Raigad MH 8.83 acres (~Rs.450cr potential); Panvel MH agreement (~Rs.1,000cr potential).
- ~25 lakh sqft of phases to be wrapped by FY31 (Vatsalya, Advik, Swarang, Aaroham).
- **Oversupply watch:** Gurugram & Pune showing early signs (heavy Gurugram launches 2 quarters running — if continues 4 more quarters, oversupply risk). Bhiwadi/Jamshedpur/Jaipur — no oversupply.
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Geographic strategy:** No new Tier-2/3 premium cities; deepen existing Jaipur/Bhiwadi (treated as extended NCR)/Jamshedpur via JVs. **Pune deepened only in Senior Living** — premium housing in Pune (Malhar) has been low-margin; "haven't figured out" decent-margin premium housing in Pune yet.
- **Gurugram:** Anmol (low-margin) was the learning project; now "bottom of top tier" of brands, aiming higher tier with premium pricing on delivery.
- **Chennai:** Aaranya (~Rs.1,800cr GDV) next to Vatsalya (Mahindra World City Chennai JDA, concluded); open to non-senior-living opportunistically.
- **Senior Living split:** ~99% of business & profit is independent/active-adult living; assisted-living/care-homes are a value-added (non-profit-focus) service — Nirmay Care Homes Bhiwadi outsourced to Epoch Elder Care; Ashiana Shubham Chennai care homes managed in-house (testing outsource vs in-house).
- **Mahindra World City:** Jaipur lease **terminated** (Mahindra couldn't get social-infra layout approvals in 18 months; door left open). Chennai live.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Senior Living is the core optionality** — 50%+ 5-yr CAGR, structural demographic thesis (aging, longevity, lower fertility, financially-independent retiring seniors in West/South/North India). Strategy: multiple price points across socio-economic segments; premiumizing (Aaranya/Tattvam more premium than legacy senior-living).
- **No annuity/leasing/services model** in medium term (5-yr) — low rental yields, lack of long-range leasing/deposit structure, seniors prefer ownership/permanence. Profits stay home-sales-led for next 5 yrs.
- **Bangalore = new geography** entry (~11 lakh sqft, ~done).
- Maharashtra Housing Policy 2025 (senior-living friendly) — intent only, rules not notified/operational yet; when live, eases scenic-parcel acquisition and adds MAHARERA senior-living marketing standards (trust-building).
margins & cost dynamics:
- Target **GP margin ~30%** (project economics gate) — for new senior-living parcels (incl. Vadgaon, Bangalore, Rs.6,500cr GDV): **gross margin 35–40%**, ~5–6% selling cost → **project-level margin 30–35%** (before corporate G&A/finance/tax).
- Cost build (% of revenue): direct costs ~60–65% (soft/approval ~5%, hard construction 40–50%, land 10–20%); outright land buys = lower land %; revenue-share = higher land %.
- PAT margin target on new projects ~15–18%.
- Margin tailwind: low land cost locked + faster execution hedges inflation → reported margins improve even as costs rise. Drag: low-margin tail projects **Ashiana Malhar Ph-II** (Pune) and **Anmol Ph-III** (Gurugram) deliver in FY27 → quarterly margin volatility, but full-year FY27>FY26>... improving.
- Construction cost +8–10% expected FY27.
capex / expansion (land acquisition — wa:
- Capital deployment intent: **deploy bulk into growth (mostly Senior Living)**, not return to shareholders; keep cash for opportunistic large Gurugram deals.
- Recent BD (last ~3 months): Panvel + Vadgaon (28.5 acres, ~20 lakh sqft, ~Rs.1,800–2,000cr GDV) + Wavarle = ~Rs.3,500cr GDV in Bombay-Pune.
- No land-banking philosophy: design→approvals→launch fast; project cycle 5–6 yrs.
- **Slippage risks flagged by mgmt:** delivery timelines, material supply, execution scale-up, labor shortages; launch timing of Oma/Aaroham Ph-III/Tattvam/Aaranya gates FY30/FY31 build-up.
capital allocation (net debt, dividends):
- **Low debt, high cash** — construction self-funded by customer advances; need-based construction funding only. ROE is the single most important metric.
- **No large buybacks/large dividends** — capital to growth. Dividends to grow in absolute terms but modest.
- IFC Rs.100cr listed NCDs (Aaroham Gurugram) on books.
risks & watch-items:
- **Class-action / consumer litigation** (filed Oct '25 on a project delivered ~5–6 yrs ago): company contesting class-action applicability in Delhi High Court (expects favorable, possibly this FY); consumer-forum matter continues regardless, could "go for years." Mgmt admits it "doesn't add up" given high NPS/satisfaction — reputational watch-item.
- Oversupply signs in Gurugram & Pune (monitor next 2–4 quarters).
- Construction cost inflation (+8–10%), material supply, labor shortages, approval delays.
- Senior-living execution risks (own words): excess competition, biting off more than can chew, managerial bandwidth across many projects, wrong market choices (Jaipur senior-living underperformed vs Chennai outperformed).
- Pune premium-housing economics still unsolved.
- Realization optics: Q4 Rs.11,566 is Gurugram-inflated, not run-rate (~Rs.9,000 blended).
management quality / tone: Candid, conservative, owner-operator tone. Refuses to speculate on macro/geopolitics; sticks to "factual and structural." Disciplined capital framework (ROE + ~30% GP gate, no land-banking, advance-funded construction). Transparent on weak spots (Pune premium, Malhar/Anmol low margins, Jaipur senior-living miss, litigation "doesn't add up"). Declines project-specific economics disclosure. High credibility on under-promising (FY27 pre-sales target deliberately below Aaroham-inflated FY26).
non-obvious takeaways:
- Headline FY26 Rs.2,421cr bookings is flattered by a single Rs.833cr Aaroham launch quarter — **FY27 target Rs.2,200cr signals normalization, not growth deceleration concern**; the real growth engine is senior-living (Rs.570cr→Rs.700cr+).
- The strategic identity is shifting: from Tier-2/3 premium-homes developer toward a **senior-living-led specialist** — incremental capital, land hunting, and management attention all tilt that way.
- Mahindra World City Jaipur termination is approvals-driven (relationship intact), not a strategy reversal — Chennai MWC JDA thriving (Vatsalya + Aaranya).
- Consolidated-vs-delivered revenue gap (Rs.1,140 vs Rs.988cr) explained by maintenance annuity + leftover-inventory top-up — a quiet, growing annuity layer even as mgmt rejects a leasing/annuity model for the core.
- FY27 20%+ ROE has cushion (achievable even with lower revenue if PAT margin held).
- Premiumization within senior-living (Aaranya/Tattvam) is a distinct lever from geographic expansion.

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.

hero.oneLiner: Landmark FY26 — record Rs.2,421cr bookings (+25% YoY) on a blockbuster Gurugram Aaroham launch and 71% YoY realization jump — with management decisively pivoting incremental capital into a 50%+ CAGR senior-living vertical (Rs.6,500cr GDV launch queue), funded by customer advances on a low-debt/high-cash balance sheet; P&L still POCS-lagged but FY27 set up for 20%+ reported ROE.
hero.industry: Real Estate — Residential Developer (mid-income premium + senior-living specialist)

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Ashiana Housing is a leading residential real estate developer with over 45 years of proven execution and customer trust in the Indian housing market"; snapshot cites 45+ "Legacy of Excellence", 36 ongoing projects, 8 cities and 20K+ "Happy Ashiana Families" (as on 31st March 2026).
- "India's No.1 Senior Living Brand with over 20 years of experience" — ranked No.1 in Senior Housing across India by Track2Realty, described in the 2025 accolades as the 8th time in a row for 2023-24 and "India's No 1 Senior Living 9th time in a Row ... for 2024-25".
- "Pioneer in differentiated residential ecosystems with strong positioning across Senior Living, Kid-Centric Homes, Premium Homes and Elite Homes focused on lifestyle-led community living"; presence across NCR, Jaipur, Chennai, Mumbai-Pune, Jamshedpur and other high-growth urban micro-markets.
- "Strong execution-led business model with integrated capabilities across land acquisition, project development, construction, and community management" plus an "Asset-light and disciplined growth strategy focused on sustainable expansion, capital efficiency, and balanced portfolio growth".
- Senior-living demand framed as need-based: "Demand is driven by lifestyle rather than speculative buying, supporting stronger customer stickiness", against an India 60+ population chart of 157 (2024), 192 (2030E), 224 (2035E) and 346 (2050E) millions (source: CREDAI report).

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body:
- **Geographic strategy:** No new Tier-2/3 premium cities; deepen existing Jaipur/Bhiwadi (treated as extended NCR)/Jamshedpur via JVs. **Pune deepened only in Senior Living** — premium housing in Pune (Malhar) has been low-margin; "haven't figured out" decent-margin premium housing in Pune yet.
- **Gurugram:** Anmol (low-margin) was the learning project; now "bottom of top tier" of brands, aiming higher tier with premium pricing on delivery.
- **Chennai:** Aaranya (~Rs.1,800cr GDV) next to Vatsalya (Mahindra World City Chennai JDA, concluded); open to non-senior-living opportunistically.
- **Senior Living split:** ~99% of business & profit is independent/active-adult living; assisted-living/care-homes are a value-added (non-profit-focus) service — Nirmay Care Homes Bhiwadi outsourced to Epoch Elder Care; Ashiana Shubham Chennai care homes managed in-house (testing outsource vs in-house).
- **Mahindra World City:** Jaipur lease **terminated** (Mahindra couldn't get social-infra layout approvals in 18 months; door left open). Chennai live.

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline (inventory, launches, land bank)
order_book.body:
- **Land bank ~96 lakh sqft total ≈ 4x annual throughput** (~2.5m sqft/yr). Build-up: ~26 lakh sqft on deck Pg26 + ~40 lakh sqft ongoing phases (=66) + 20 lakh sqft Vadgaon (April, =86) + ~11 lakh sqft Bangalore (MoU, CP resolved, "99% likely", =96). Management calls 4x "just enough to maintain"; **actively targeting to add more land in FY27, mainly senior-living.**
- Senior Living **launch queue: 5 projects, GDV >Rs.6,500cr** (Chennai, Bangalore, Bombay-Pune) to launch over next 12–24 months.
- FY26 land added: Chennai + Maharashtra, >26 lakh sqft, ~Rs.3,200cr sale potential.
- Q4 BD: Raigad MH 8.83 acres (~Rs.450cr potential); Panvel MH agreement (~Rs.1,000cr potential).
- ~25 lakh sqft of phases to be wrapped by FY31 (Vatsalya, Advik, Swarang, Aaroham).
- **Oversupply watch:** Gurugram & Pune showing early signs (heavy Gurugram launches 2 quarters running — if continues 4 more quarters, oversupply risk). Bhiwadi/Jamshedpur/Jaipur — no oversupply.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL)
guidance.body:
- **FY27 pre-sales target: Rs.2,200cr** (note: below FY26's Rs.2,421cr, which was Aaroham-inflated — implies normalization, not a step-up on headline).
- **Senior Living FY27 target: cross Rs.700cr** (from Rs.570cr; the strategic priority).
- **Blended realization** to drift toward ~Rs.10,000/sqft (range Rs.9,000–11,000) as senior-living mix rises and Aaranya/Tattvam premiumize.
- **FY27 reported ROE: 20%+** (on track; cushion exists even at lower revenue if PAT margin held). Margin profile: FY27 > FY26, FY28 > FY27.
- **FY30: cumulative PAT Rs.2,000cr** target — "on track."
- **New launches this FY (FY27):** Ashiana Oma (Jaipur premium, approvals done, launch in ~2 months), Ashiana Aaranya & Ashiana Tattvam (both Q4 FY27); plus phase launches — Aaroham Phase-III, and ≥1 phase each in Advik, Amodh, Vatsalya, Swarang.
- **FY28 launches:** Wavarle, Vadgaon, Bangalore.
- Construction-cost guidance: **+8–10% YoY** in FY27 (higher than historical CPI; geopolitics-driven).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Senior Living is the core optionality** — 50%+ 5-yr CAGR, structural demographic thesis (aging, longevity, lower fertility, financially-independent retiring seniors in West/South/North India). Strategy: multiple price points across socio-economic segments; premiumizing (Aaranya/Tattvam more premium than legacy senior-living).
- **No annuity/leasing/services model** in medium term (5-yr) — low rental yields, lack of long-range leasing/deposit structure, seniors prefer ownership/permanence. Profits stay home-sales-led for next 5 yrs.
- **Bangalore = new geography** entry (~11 lakh sqft, ~done).
- Maharashtra Housing Policy 2025 (senior-living friendly) — intent only, rules not notified/operational yet; when live, eases scenic-parcel acquisition and adds MAHARERA senior-living marketing standards (trust-building).

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- Target **GP margin ~30%** (project economics gate) — for new senior-living parcels (incl. Vadgaon, Bangalore, Rs.6,500cr GDV): **gross margin 35–40%**, ~5–6% selling cost → **project-level margin 30–35%** (before corporate G&A/finance/tax).
- Cost build (% of revenue): direct costs ~60–65% (soft/approval ~5%, hard construction 40–50%, land 10–20%); outright land buys = lower land %; revenue-share = higher land %.
- PAT margin target on new projects ~15–18%.
- Margin tailwind: low land cost locked + faster execution hedges inflation → reported margins improve even as costs rise. Drag: low-margin tail projects **Ashiana Malhar Ph-II** (Pune) and **Anmol Ph-III** (Gurugram) deliver in FY27 → quarterly margin volatility, but full-year FY27>FY26>... improving.
- Construction cost +8–10% expected FY27.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation (net debt, dividends)
capital_allocation.body:
- **Low debt, high cash** — construction self-funded by customer advances; need-based construction funding only. ROE is the single most important metric.
- **No large buybacks/large dividends** — capital to growth. Dividends to grow in absolute terms but modest.
- IFC Rs.100cr listed NCDs (Aaroham Gurugram) on books.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Candid, conservative, owner-operator tone. Refuses to speculate on macro/geopolitics; sticks to "factual and structural." Disciplined capital framework (ROE + ~30% GP gate, no land-banking, advance-funded construction). Transparent on weak spots (Pune premium, Malhar/Anmol low margins, Jaipur senior-living miss, litigation "doesn't add up"). Declines project-specific economics disclosure. High credibility on under-promising (FY27 pre-sales target deliberately below Aaroham-inflated FY26).

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Class-action / consumer litigation** (filed Oct '25 on a project delivered ~5–6 yrs ago): company contesting class-action applicability in Delhi High Court (expects favorable, possibly this FY); consumer-forum matter continues regardless, could "go for years." Mgmt admits it "doesn't add up" given high NPS/satisfaction — reputational watch-item.
- Oversupply signs in Gurugram & Pune (monitor next 2–4 quarters).
- Construction cost inflation (+8–10%), material supply, labor shortages, approval delays.
- Senior-living execution risks (own words): excess competition, biting off more than can chew, managerial bandwidth across many projects, wrong market choices (Jaipur senior-living underperformed vs Chennai outperformed).
- Pune premium-housing economics still unsolved.
- Realization optics: Q4 Rs.11,566 is Gurugram-inflated, not run-rate (~Rs.9,000 blended).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- Headline FY26 Rs.2,421cr bookings is flattered by a single Rs.833cr Aaroham launch quarter — **FY27 target Rs.2,200cr signals normalization, not growth deceleration concern**; the real growth engine is senior-living (Rs.570cr→Rs.700cr+).
- The strategic identity is shifting: from Tier-2/3 premium-homes developer toward a **senior-living-led specialist** — incremental capital, land hunting, and management attention all tilt that way.
- Mahindra World City Jaipur termination is approvals-driven (relationship intact), not a strategy reversal — Chennai MWC JDA thriving (Vatsalya + Aaranya).
- Consolidated-vs-delivered revenue gap (Rs.1,140 vs Rs.988cr) explained by maintenance annuity + leftover-inventory top-up — a quiet, growing annuity layer even as mgmt rejects a leasing/annuity model for the core.
- FY27 20%+ ROE has cushion (achievable even with lower revenue if PAT margin held).
- Premiumization within senior-living (Aaranya/Tattvam) is a distinct lever from geographic expansion.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)
challenges.body:
> Only challenges specifically discussed on the call.

| Challenge | Beneficiary — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Industry consolidation toward branded/financially-disciplined developers (resilient demand, premiumization) | Ashiana — ASHIANA · 523716 · Real Estate (branded, low-debt, execution track record) | Unorganized / leveraged small developers | Mgmt explicitly: consolidation benefits disciplined players with execution + positioning. ✅ |
| Gurugram & Pune early oversupply (heavy launches) | — | Developers with high unsold Gurugram/Pune inventory | Absolute unsold inventory up 2 quarters in Gurugram; risk if persists 4 more quarters. Ashiana relatively insulated (advance-funded, diversified). ⭐ (early signal) |

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this):** Record FY — bookings Rs.2,421cr (+25% YoY), Q4 Rs.1,290cr (+124% YoY) on Aaroham Gurugram launch (Rs.833cr); realization Q4 Rs.11,566 (+71% YoY), FY ~Rs.9,000; collections Rs.1,762cr (ATH); op cash flow Rs.577cr (+34%, ATH); PAT Rs.118cr (vs Rs.18cr FY25). Senior Living Rs.570cr (+55%). Land bank ~96 lakh sqft (~4x). Senior-living launch queue Rs.6,500cr GDV. FY27 guidance: pre-sales Rs.2,200cr, senior-living >Rs.700cr, 20%+ ROE; launches Oma/Aaranya/Tattvam + Aaroham Ph-III. New BD: Vadgaon, Panvel, Raigad, Wavarle, Bangalore. IFC Rs.100cr NCDs; Maitri Kolkata settled (Rs.18.5cr). MWC Jaipur lease terminated. Class-action litigation contested in Delhi HC. Oversupply signs flagged Gurugram/Pune.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Land litigation] "Milakpur Land, with estimated area 40.63 Acres and potential Saleable area 31 Lakh sq. ft., is under acquisition and company's writ petition is pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Rajasthan against acquisition." It is excluded from the 67.09-acre future-development table.
- [JV] "Ashiana Swarang is acquired by Kairav Developers Ltd. (a joint venture company with equal economic interest of Ashiana Housing Ltd. and Arihant Foundations" — Swarang's three ongoing phases are carried at 50% of the profits.
- [Phasing restatement] "In some of the projects, saleable area has been updated as per latest/revised phasing plan", so future-project areas are not comparable across decks.
- [Awards] 2025 Track2Realty rankings beyond senior housing: No.3 in North India across asset class, No.5 CSR brand PAN India, No.9 Real Estate Employer, No.10 Residential Segment; Amodh named Senior Living Project of the Year 2025 at the ET Real Estate Awards (National Edition).
- [IR] Presentation prepared by Valorem Advisors, an independent investor relations management service company, which certifies its directors/employees own no stock in the company.
